root_cause.text: The atmel-aes buffer cleanup routine in `drivers/crypto/atmel-aes.c` freed a multi-page allocation with `free_page()` instead of `free_pages(..., ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER)`, so only the first page of the 4-page buffer was released and the other 3 pages leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message states `atmel_aes_buff_init()` allocates 4 pages using `__get_free_pages()` with `ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER`, while `atmel_aes_buff_cleanup()` “frees only the first page using free_page(), leaking the remaining 3 pages”; the patch changes `free_page((unsigned long)dd->buf);` to `free_pages((unsigned long)dd->buf, ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix buffer cleanup to free the AES buffer with the correct page order.
intent_record.what: In atmel_aes_buff_cleanup(), the deallocation call was changed from free_page((unsigned long)dd->buf) to free_pages((unsigned long)dd->buf, ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER).
intent_record.how: The buffer is now freed using the same page order it was likely allocated with, so multi-page allocations are released correctly instead of being treated as a single page.

grouping_result.intent: Fix buffer cleanup to free the AES buffer with the correct page order.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes AES buffer cleanup to release the multi-page allocation with the correct page order instead of freeing only a single page.

candidates.rationale: This cleanup frees only a single page from a buffer that was allocated across multiple pages, leaving the remaining pages unreleased and causing a memory leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This cleanup call releases only one page even though the AES buffer was allocated as a multi-page buffer, so the remaining pages are not freed, causing the memory leak described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable cleanup routine is present in this snippet. The function `static void atmel_aes_buff_cleanup(struct atmel_aes_dev *dd)` contains `free_page((unsigned long)dd->buf);`, while the buffer was allocated with `__get_free_pages(GFP_KERNEL, ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER);` in `atmel_aes_buff_init()`. Since the allocation is multi-page (`ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER`), using `free_page()` only frees one page and leaks the remaining pages. The fix is not present here because the cleanup still uses `free_page()` rather than `free_pages(..., ATMEL_AES_BUFFER_ORDER)`.
